???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What kind of rule, such as an index being inside its array, depends on values known only while the program runs?"

        A dynamic rule. Unless the compiler can prove the answer, it keeps a runtime check for it.

        Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#14-static-and-dynamic-rules).

    ??? question "What do we call a program that satisfies every applicable v0.1 rule?"

        Well-formed. A conforming compiler must accept it, within its documented limits.

        Introduced in [5. Types and language rules](stage-5-types-and-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#12-programs).

    ??? question "For a compiler, what is the material for one test usually made of, and what is it called?"

        A test case, one Vortex source file together with a description of what should happen to it.

        Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

    ??? question "What does the compiler place in generated code just before an operation that might fail, such as dividing by a variable?"

        A runtime check. It may be left out only when the compiler can prove the operation safe.

        Introduced in [Learn: 8. Runtime and numerical rules](../../language-tour/06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#14-static-and-dynamic-rules).

    ??? question "What happens when a running Vortex program divides an integer by zero?"

        A runtime error. The program stops and reports what went wrong.

        Introduced in [Learn: 8. Runtime and numerical rules](../../language-tour/06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#runtime-error).
